# Paraguay

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −1.14, by age as below | MICS 2016, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −1.03 | DHS 1990, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | −1.24 (95% prediction interval −1.98 to −0.51) | [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md) at GDP per capita (PPP, constant 2021 international $) of $17,246 (2025, World Bank) |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.91 | −1.24 | −0.93 | −0.81 | −1.04 | −1.53 | −2.12 |

**Adult and child mortality gradient by age** (`mort_gradient`; ages 15–59: the 45q15 gradient above plus the pooled offset for each band ([age pattern](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)); ages 5–14 use the 15–29 value; ages 60–74 fall in a straight line from the 45–59 value to 0 at age 75; ages 75 and above, and OG-Core's final age, use 0):

| 1–4 | 5–14 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | 75+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.75 (DHS 1990) | −1.65 | −1.65 | −1.42 | −1.04 | −1.04 at 60, falling to 0 at 75 | 0 |

Ages 1–4 use the country's own gradient in child mortality at ages 1–4 (DHS), or, where there is none, its under-five gradient plus a pooled offset ([details](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)). Infant mortality (age 0) is `infmort_gradient`, above.

*Note:* The most recent survey with infant mortality by wealth quintile is from 1990. Gradients can change substantially over such a period; state the survey year when using this value.

## Estimates

### Household surveys

Latest Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) or Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) with a complete wealth-quintile breakdown, for each indicator ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv); earlier surveys in `gradient_library.csv`). MICS rates are taken from the World Bank's compilation of survey results by wealth quintile ([sources](../sources.md)).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total fertility rate (births per woman) | MICS 2016 | 4.1 | 3.1 | 2.3 | 2.1 | 1.6 | 2.56 | −1.14 |
| Infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 1990 | 43 | 36 | 46 | 33 | 16 | 2.69 | −1.03 |
| Under-five mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 1990 | 57 | 50 | 59 | 39 | 20 | 2.85 | −1.17 |
| Child mortality, ages 1–4 (per 1,000 children aged 1) | DHS 1990 | 15 | 14 | 14 | 6 | 4 | 3.75 | −1.75 |
